angle_en: the self is untouched even while in the body
angle_hi: आत्मा शरीर में रहते हुए भी अछूती रहती है

en.intro: Krishna has just described the source of all expansion. Now he asks you to look at the self that lives inside the body. What is its nature?
en.notice: The verse tells you this self is beginningless and beyond the gunas, and even while it lives in a body, it does not act and is not stained.
en.next: Krishna explains that just as space is untouched by what happens within it, the self remains pure in every body.
en.meaning: O son of Kunti, this supreme self is beginningless, beyond the gunas, and imperishable. Though abiding in the body, it does not act and is not stained.

hi.intro: कृष्ण ने विस्तार का स्रोत बताया, अब वे उस आत्मा को देखने को कहते हैं जो शरीर में रहती है। उसकी क्या प्रकृति है?
hi.meaning: हे कुन्तीनन्दन, यह परमात्मा स्वयं अनादि और गुणों से रहित होने के कारण अव्यय है। यह शरीर में रहते हुए भी न करता है और न लिप्त होता है।
hi.notice: यह आत्मा अनादि है, गुणों से परे है, और शरीर में रहने पर भी न तो कार्य करती है और न ही उसका कोई कलंक लगता है।
hi.next: जैसे आकाश सूक्ष्म होने के कारण अछूता रहता है, वैसे ही आत्मा हर शरीर में रहकर भी अछूती रहती है।

en.intro: Krishna has just described the source of all expansion. Now he asks you to look at the self that lives inside the body. What is its nature?
en.body: O son of Kunti, this supreme self is beginningless, beyond the gunas, and imperishable. Though abiding in the body, it does not act and is not stained. The verse tells you this self is beginningless and beyond the gunas, and even while it lives in a body, it does not act and is not stained. Krishna explains that just as space is untouched by what happens within it, the self remains pure in every body.

issues: meaning_changed: "यह परमात्मा स्वयं अनादि और गुणों से रहित होने के कारण अविनाशी है।" (The Hindi meaning drops the explicit word 'अव्ययः' (imperishable) and replaces it with 'अविनाशी' (indestructible/cannot be destroyed). While related, 'अव्ययः' specifically implies imperishability or not being depleted, which is a distinct nuance from 'अविनाशी' (indestructible). This is a semantic shift in the attribute of the self.)
